objective_for_doctor: A 23-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: shortness of breath.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’ve been having shortness of breath or difficulty breathing in a significant way, and I’m also consulting because I have high blood pressure.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the shortness of breath start, and is it worse with exertion, lying flat, or at night? Any chest pain, fever, cough, or wheezing?  
Doctor: Also, do you have leg swelling or pain, do you smoke or use vaping, and what’s your blood pressure reading and any medications you take?

I don’t know. I can say that I have had pericarditis, and I have shortness of breath or difficulty breathing in a significant way. I also have pain somewhere related to the reason for consulting (pain intensity 5/10, sharp and sensitive), and my pain locations include the back of the neck, ankles (right and left), knee (right), and shoulder (left). The pain doesn’t radiate anywhere. I also have red lesions/redness on my skin that I believe are related to the condition I’m consulting for.

Doctor: Thanks—do the red skin lesions look like a rash or blotches (any itching), and is there chest pain that’s worse when you breathe in or lie down? Also, since you have prior pericarditis, have you had any recent ECG/echocardiogram results, and do you have a current temperature or cough?

Yes—there are red lesions/redness on my skin that I believe are related to the condition I’m consulting for. The rash itching severity is 3/10. I don’t know about a temperature, a cough, or any recent ECG/echocardiogram results. I also don’t know about chest pain that’s worse when you breathe in or lie down.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—are the red lesions flat or raised, do they appear suddenly and spread, and have you noticed any mouth ulcers, joint swelling, or numbness/tingling? Also, is your shortness of breath constant or episodic, and do you have a measured pulse-ox or oxygen saturation?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG and transthoracic echocardiogram  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR/CRP, BMP, and urinalysis (protein/hematuria)

Doctor: I understand—you don’t know the specifics yet; I need a few key details: is the rash worse with sun exposure and do you have mouth sores, and is the shortness of breath sudden or gradual? Also, any recent weight loss, fatigue, or new medications?

I don’t know. I do have red lesions/redness on my skin that I believe are related to the condition I’m consulting for, and the rash itching severity is 3/10. I also have shortness of breath or difficulty breathing in a significant way.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since you don’t know timing details, please tell me: do the red lesions blanch when you press them, and are they on areas exposed to sunlight or more on the palms/soles? Also, is your shortness of breath sudden (minutes-hours) or gradual (days-weeks), and do you have any wheeze or cough.

I don’t know about whether the red lesions blanch when you press them, and I don’t know whether they’re on sun-exposed areas versus more on the palms or soles. I also don’t know whether my shortness of breath is sudden or gradual, and I don’t know if I have wheeze or cough.
